# Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped

          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate

# Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi

          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:

# Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

We write answers to pty.write(). 

Actually simpler and closer to AC2: spawn `sh` directly with stdin as the PIPE? No — the wizard reads from /dev/tty when stdin isn't a tty. So: spawn the shell with stdin=pipe (so `[ -t 0 ]` false → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty), stdout/stderr=pipe for capture, and give the process a CONTROLLING TTY so /dev/tty exists. pty2's PseudoTerminal.start gives the child the pty as controlling terminal AND as stdin/stdout/stderr by default... If stdin IS the tty, then `[ -t 0 ]` true → FAH_TTY=/dev/stdin — reads come from the pty anyway. Either path works: we feed via pty.write, capture via pty.out (stdout+stderr merged? pty merges them by nature of the tty).

The AC2 form `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'` matters: it exercises the PIPED mode (stdin not a tty → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty). changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Good. `pty2` package exists. For the wizard IT tests I don't need the full xterm harness — I just need a pty for /dev/tty. The wizard reads from `$FAH_TTY` (=/dev/tty when stdin isn't a tty). With pty2, `PseudoTerminal.start('/bin/dash', ['-c', 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'])`... hmm wait — under `dash -c 'cat file | dash'`, stdin of the inner dash is the pipe; /dev/tty resolves to the pty slave of the SESSION — pty2 gives the child a controlling terminal, so /dev/tty = the pty. We write answers to pty.write(). 

Actually simpler and closer to AC2: spawn `sh` directly with stdin as the PIPE? No — the wizard reads from /dev/tty when stdin isn't a tty. So: spawn the shell with stdin=pipe (so `[ -t 0 ]` false → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty), stdout/stderr=pipe for capture, and give the process a CONTROLLING TTY so /dev/tty exists. pty2's PseudoTerminal.start gives the child the pty as controlling terminal AND as stdin/stdout/stderr by default... Does pty2 support separate stdin? Let me check pty2's API: `PseudoTerminal.start(executable, args, workingDirectory, environment, raw)` — probably wires the pty to all three fds. If stdin IS the tty, then `[ -t 0 ]` true → FAH_TTY=/dev/stdin — reads come from the pty anyway. Either path works: we feed via pty.write, capture via pty.out (stdout+stderr merged? pty merges them by nature of the tty).

The AC2 form `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'` matters: it exercises the PIPED mode (stdin not a tty → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty). With pty2's default (pty on stdio), stdin is a tty → takes the /dev/stdin branch — that's the `bash site/setup.sh` direct path (AC5/IT-3), not the piped path. To exercise the piped path under a controlling tty, I can run `dash -c 'exec dash site/setup.sh < /dev/null ...'`? Hmm.

Piped semantics: `cat site/setup.sh | dash` — dash's stdin = pipe (the script text). The script's `[ -t 0 ]` → false → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty. So I need: shell stdin = a pipe containing the script; controlling terminal exists for /dev/tty; stdout/stderr captured.

Options with pty2: start a wrapper shell attached to the pty that runs the pipeline INSIDE: e.g. run via the pty: `/bin/dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | /bin/dash'` — then the OUTER dash has the pty on stdio; the INNER dash's stdin is the pipe → [ -t 0 ] false → /dev/tty = the session's controlling tty = the pty. Answers via pty.write. stdout of the inner dash → inherits the outer's stdout → the pty → captured via pty.out. 

For IT-4 (non-TTY): `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'` with NO pty at all (Process.start with pipes): stdin pipe (script via cat? no — inner dash stdin is the pipe carrying the script), stderr captured. /dev/tty may EXIST on the test runner (the dart test process itself might have a controlling terminal? In CI, no; locally, yes!). If /dev/tty exists but is not... the guard is `[ ! -e /dev/tty ] || [ ! -t 2 ]` — stderr not a tty → guard fires regardless of /dev/tty existence. With Process.start pipes, stderr is a pipe → `[ ! -t 2 ]` true → guard fires. So IT-4 doesn't need a pty even locally: `sh -c 'cat site/setup.sh | sh'` with all stdio piped. 

For bash direct (IT-3/AC5): `bash site/setup.sh` with pty on stdio (stdin IS tty → /dev/stdin branch).

But — the wizard checks `command -v fa`! IT needs a fake `fa` on PATH (fixture shim). And the persist step asks about `$SHELL` rc — with SHELL unset, `shell_rc` stays empty → manual instructions, no rc write. Fixture: leave SHELL unset → key lands nowhere; assert transcript free of key. But then "exactly once" assertion... I could set SHELL=/bin/bash and answer 'n' to persist → assert key appears nowhere in $HOME; or answer 'y' → assert `~/.bashrc` contains it exactly once. The strongest IT (AC3 spirit): run one flavor with persist=y and assert exactly-once in the rc + zero in transcript; other flavors answer 'n'.

Hmm wait — also `grep -qF "export KEY="` on the rc file and `sed -i.bak` — sed -i.bak works on darwin (BSD sed needs the suffix arg — `-i.bak` form works on both GNU and BSD!). Actually BSD sed: `sed -i.bak 's|...|...|'` — the `.bak` suffix form is portable. OK.

And the `fa` shim: `command -v fa` finds it, then `ok "Found 'fa' on PATH ($(command -v fa ...))"`. Fine with a stub script that echoes something.

Also the HOME: fixture HOME temp dir; wizard writes $HOME/.fah/config.yaml.

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set — live on
      # pull_request events AND on SM validation dispatches: the paths
      # step derives the validated diff from merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)
      # when no pull_request context exists (fail-safe — a classification
      # failure runs the leg, never skips it).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # Issue #1267 N2: the diff modified flutter_app/pubspec.lock — the
      # transitive-drift vector that kept linux/windows release builds red
      # for five nights (#1265). Same path-triggered model as exzone.
      locksmoke: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.locksmoke }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read; git
          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
      # Non-PR events (tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards releases. Since gh-1537
      # there are NO main-push events at all; the SM validation dispatch
      # (workflow_dispatch on the rebased PR head) is the pre-merge gate
      # and lands in this arm, so every validation runs the whole-tree
      # gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd) — nothing was
      # ever main-only.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi

          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:

- environment: base (TERM, LANG + copied LOGNAME/USER/DISPLAY/LC_TYPE/HOME/PATH) then `environment:` OVERRIDES. SHELL is NOT inherited ✓ (no SHELL in the copy list) — so the wizard sees NO SHELL by default → shell_rc empty → manual instructions. For the persist-yes flavor: environment: {'SHELL': '/bin/bash'} ✓.
- HOME: inherited from parent unless overridden — I ALWAYS override HOME ✓. For the HOME-unset test: override with '' (empty) ✓.
- exitCode: `Future<int> get exitCode` ✓ available — no exit-file hack needed.
- raw:false → canonical mode, ECHO ON (default), ICRNL ON. Answers written as '...\r' → translated to '\n' ✓. ECHO ON — typed bytes echo → the KEY must only be sent after `read -s` disabled echo (the prompt-wait + small delay handles it).
- The executable resolution: PATH search from the EFFECTIVE env ✓.

One more concern: in canonical mode, when the child prints the prompt "Pick a provider [1-13] \033[0m " WITHOUT a trailing newline (prompt ends with a space), my wait-for-text must match a substring (not line-based) ✓ I'll match on the raw accumulated buffer (ANSI-stripped).

Also the wizard's `ok "Found 'fa' on PATH (...)"` prints path — fine.

Timing: canonical mode buffers input — I can safely send the next answer only after the next prompt appears. For HIDDEN read: after "Paste your" + 150ms delay, send key.

Now — one subtle thing about the piped invocation under pty: `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'`. The OUTER dash runs on the pty (its stdin IS the tty → but the outer only runs cat+pipeline, no reads). The INNER dash: stdin=pipe from cat ✓ [ -t 0 ] false → FAH_TTY=/dev/tty ✓. /dev/tty = controlling terminal = the pty ✓ (openlogin_tty set by login_tty in pty fork) ✓.

For bash DIRECT: `bash site/setup.sh` — wait, the script has a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang; running `bash script` explicitly ✓ (AC5 form).

busybox: `busybox ash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | busybox ash'` — hmm, `cat` inside: busybox ash redirects... use plain `cat` (coreutils present) — fine. Or `busybox ash script` directly? Piped form is the AC2 target: `busybox ash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | busybox ash'` ✓.

Exit codes: `cat x | dash` — pipeline status = last (dash) ✓. On SIGINT: inner dash killed → status 130 ✓... outer dash -c waits → exitCode of outer = 130 ✓.

Also — IMPORTANT — will `set -e` + SIGINT... fine.

Timing: each IT run does ~8 prompt round-trips; each wait ≤ a few seconds. 4 runs + extras — a few minutes max. @Timeout(5min) ok. Add skip logic:

```dart
bool _have(String bin) => Process.runSync('sh', ['-c', 'command -v $bin']).exitCode == 0;
```

Now — models/urls sanity for the 13 providers: zai baseUrl 'https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4' etc. — pulled from catalog ✓ no hardcoding.

Let me now write all the files. Order:
1. test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart (UT-1 + AC6) — RED (template has printf -v; data sections stale).
2. test/site/installer_golden_test.dart (UT-2) — RED (renderInstallers doesn't exist yet — compile error counts as RED).

11. CI: classifier output + jobs + quality-gate.
12. Run tests, analyze, ledger, response.md.

One more check — `knownModelPresets` keys: openrouter, kimi, anthropic, google, openai. kimi's presets include 'k3' etc. — the wizard's kimi menu: 1) k3 (recommended) 2) kimi-for-coding 3) kimi-for-coding-highspeed 4) k3-256k 5) other. Hmm — is k3 the right recommended? It's the CLI's own fallback list order — "presets = current recommended defaults" ✓ generated, not my call.

Now — about `install-config.yaml` `modes:` — generated mode menus reference `ask mode` → `mode=$(ask "Pick a mode" "1")` ✓.

```sh

    say ""
