{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pty2 unix impl:

SHELL is NOT inherited ✓ (no SHELL in the copy list) — so the wizard sees NO SHELL by default → shell_rc empty → manual instructions. For the persist-yes flavor: environment: {'SHELL': '/bin/bash'} ✓.
- HOME: inherited from parent unless overridden — I ALWAYS override HOME ✓. For the HOME-unset test: override with '' (empty) ✓.
- exitCode: `Future<int> get exitCode` ✓ available — no exit-file hack needed.
- raw:false → canonical mode, ECHO ON (default), ICRNL ON. Answers written as '...\r' → translated to '\n' ✓. ECHO ON — typed bytes echo → the KEY must only be sent after `read -s` disabled echo (the prompt-wait + small delay handles it).
- The executable resolution: PATH search from the EFFECTIVE env ✓.

One more concern: in canonical mode, when the child prints the prompt "Pick a provider [1-13] \033[0m " WITHOUT a trailing newline (prompt ends with a space), my wait-for-text must match a substring (not line-based) ✓ I'll match on the raw accumulated buffer (ANSI-stripped).

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

}

ask() {
  local var="$1" text="$2" default="${3:-}"
  while true; do
    if [ -n "$default" ]; then
      prompt "$text [$default]"
    else
      prompt "$text"
    fi
    local value
    if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
      value=$default
    fi
    printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
    return 0
  done
}

ask_hidden() {
  local var="$1" text="$2"
  prompt "$text"
  local value
  if ! read -rs value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf -v "$var" ''
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
  return 0
}

My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"
  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"
  printf 'baseUrl: %s\n' "$base_url"
  printf 'mode: %s\n' "$mode"
  printf 'approvalMode: %s\n' "$approval"
  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""
ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","oldText":"# Write config.yaml

provider: ${provider_kind}

approvalMode: ${approval}
allowedTools: []
EOF
ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","path":"site/setup.sh.template"}

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

    fi

}

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prompt() {

}

ask() {
  local var="$1" text="$2" default="${3:-}"

    if [ -n "$default" ]; then
      prompt "$text [$default]"
    else
      prompt "$text"
    fi
    local value
    if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
      value=$default
    fi
    printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
    return 0
  done
}

ask_hidden() {
  local var="$1" text="$2"
  prompt "$text"
  local value
  if ! read -rs value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf -v "$var" ''
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
  return 0
}

    else

    fi

}","path":"site/setup.sh.template"}

blocks.text: Edited site/setup.sh.template: replaced 1455 bytes with 1979 bytes.

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

Now the non-TTY guard (exit 0 → 1), the reconfigure/needs_key/persist call sites, and the atomic config write.

{"newText":"# ── 2. Interactive configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# AC4 (gh-1596): a non-TTY run (piped CI, curl|sh without a terminal) cannot
# collect answers — print the guidance and exit NON-ZERO so callers never
# read the run as a completed setup.
if [ ! -e /dev/tty ] || [ ! -t 2 ]; then
  info "Non-interactive environment detected."
  say ""
  say "  To finish setup, set an API key and run:"
  say ""
  say "    fa"
  say ""
  exit 1
fi

if [ -f "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
  reconfigure=$(ask_yn "A config already exists at ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}. Reconfigure?" "n")
  if [ "$reconfigure" != "y" ]; then
    ok "Kept existing config. Run 'fa' to start."
    exit 0
  fi
fi","oldText":"# ── 2. Interactive configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"
  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"
  printf 'baseUrl: %s\n' "$base_url"
  printf 'mode: %s\n' "$mode"
  printf 'approvalMode: %s\n' "$approval"
  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""
ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","oldText":"# Write config.yaml

ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","path":"site/setup.sh.template"}

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).

{"newText":"# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.

  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"' EXIT","oldText":"set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
      value=$default
    fi

ask_hidden() {

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).

FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"
  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"
  printf 'baseUrl: %s\n' "$base_url"
  printf 'mode: %s\n' "$mode"
  printf 'approvalMode: %s\n' "$approval"
  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

Now the non-TTY guard (exit 0 → 1), the reconfigure/needs_key/persist call sites, and the atomic config write.

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

    fi

ask_hidden() {

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"
  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"
  printf 'baseUrl: %s\n' "$base_url"
  printf 'mode: %s\n' "$mode"
  printf 'approvalMode: %s\n' "$approval"
  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

    fi

ask_hidden() {

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

Now the non-TTY guard (exit 0 → 1), the reconfigure/needs_key/persist call sites, and the atomic config write.

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).

FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{

  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"

  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

    fi

}

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done

Actually — Dart's `File.readAsStringSync` documentation: "The BOM... is stripped"? Let me recall: package `File.readAs*` uses utf8.decode which DOES consume a leading U+FEFF? There IS a known behavior: `Utf8Codec.decode` does not strip BOM, but `File.readAsStringSync`... The empirical result stands: committed length 8367 (without BOM char? the xxd says the file HAS 3 BOM bytes: 8368 bytes → decoded chars = 8367 if BOM stripped... rendered string length 8368 (includes BOM char). {"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

    fi

}

ask_hidden() {
  local var="$1" text="$2"
  prompt "$text"
  local value
  if ! read -rs value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf -v "$var" ''

  fi

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

}

      prompt "$text [$default]"
    else
      prompt "$text"
    fi
    local value
    if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
      value=$default
    fi
    printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
    return 0
  done
}

ask_hidden() {
  local var="$1" text="$2"
  prompt "$text"
  local value
  if ! read -rs value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf -v "$var" ''
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
  return 0
}

}","path":"site/setup.sh.template"}

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

Now the non-TTY guard (exit 0 → 1), the reconfigure/needs_key/persist call sites, and the atomic config write.

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

blocks.text: Edited site/setup.sh.template: replaced 1455 bytes with 1979 bytes.

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

Now the non-TTY guard (exit 0 → 1), the reconfigure/needs_key/persist call sites, and the atomic config write.

{"newText":"# ── 2. Interactive configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────

  say ""

{"newText":"# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"
  printf 'model: %s\n' "$model"
  printf 'baseUrl: %s\n' "$base_url"
  printf 'mode: %s\n' "$mode"
  printf 'approvalMode: %s\n' "$approval"
  printf 'allowedTools: []\n'
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""
ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","oldText":"# Write config.yaml

ok "Wrote ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}"","path":"site/setup.sh.template"}

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

}

  local var="$1" text="$2" default="${3:-}"
  while true; do
    if [ -n "$default" ]; then
      prompt "$text [$default]"
    else
      prompt "$text"
    fi
    local value
    if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
      value=$default
    fi
    printf -v "$var" '%s' "$value"
    return 0
  done
}

ask_hidden() {
  local var="$1" text="$2"
  prompt "$text"
  local value
  if ! read -rs value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf -v "$var" ''
    return 1

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Wait — the original `ask` had a `while true; do ... done` loop that was functionally a no-op (all paths return). I removed it — but hold on, one subtle behavior: the original loop re-prompted? No — every branch returns, so the loop ran once. Removal is behavior-identical ✓.

But WAIT — a critical difference in the original `ask`: on EOF it did `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` (assigned the default) and returned 1 → set -e aborted. My new version prints the default to stdout and returns 1 → the caller `var=$(ask ...)` gets the default but the assignment FAILS (exit 1) → set -e aborts ✓ same net effect.

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}","oldText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"newText":"# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # read's EOF behavior assigns the empty string to the named variable, so
  # the failure path below never needs `eval` (and never echoes the value).
  if ! read -rs "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  return 0
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
