concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is

  # The ubuntu leg carries the curl|sh dialects (dash = Ubuntu sh, busybox

  # macOS sh is bash 3.2 POSIX mode, the shell that never saw the #1596

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml')
t = p.read_text()

# 1) needs list: insert installer-portability before installer-verify (keeps the
#    pinned needs tail "install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]" intact)
old = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
new = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 2) report line
old = "          echo \"installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}\""
new = old + "\n          echo \"installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}\""
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 3) env var
old = "          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
new = old + "\n          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 4) kv loop: insert before the LAST pair so the pinned tail stays last
old = '                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \\'
new = '                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \\\n' + old
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 5) platform class: append to the parenthetical (pinned substring intact)
old = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)"
new = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

p.write_text(t)
print("quality-gate wiring applied (5 points)")
EOF"}

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# declares its own job-level permissions block.

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'

    permissions:
      contents: read

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml')
t = p.read_text()

# 1) needs list: insert installer-portability before installer-verify (keeps the
#    pinned needs tail "install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]" intact)
old = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
new = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 2) report line
old = "          echo \"installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}\""
new = old + "\n          echo \"installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}\""
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 3) env var
old = "          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
new = old + "\n          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 4) kv loop: insert before the LAST pair so the pinned tail stays last
old = '                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \\'
new = '                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \\\n' + old
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 5) platform class: append to the parenthetical (pinned substring intact)
old = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)"
new = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

p.write_text(t)
print("quality-gate wiring applied (5 points)")
EOF"}

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# declares its own job-level permissions block.

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml')
t = p.read_text()

# 1) needs list: insert installer-portability before installer-verify (keeps the
#    pinned needs tail "install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]" intact)
old = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
new = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 2) report line
old = "          echo \"installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}\""
new = old + "\n          echo \"installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}\""
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 3) env var
old = "          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
new = old + "\n          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 4) kv loop: insert before the LAST pair so the pinned tail stays last
old = '                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \\'
new = '                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \\\n' + old
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 5) platform class: append to the parenthetical (pinned substring intact)
old = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)"
new = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

p.write_text(t)
print("quality-gate wiring applied (5 points)")
EOF"}

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml')
t = p.read_text()

# 1) needs list: insert installer-portability before installer-verify (keeps the
#    pinned needs tail "install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]" intact)
old = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
new = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 2) report line
old = "          echo \"installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}\""
new = old + "\n          echo \"installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}\""
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 3) env var
old = "          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
new = old + "\n          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 4) kv loop: insert before the LAST pair so the pinned tail stays last
old = '                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \\'
new = '                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \\\n' + old
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 5) platform class: append to the parenthetical (pinned substring intact)
old = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)"
new = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

p.write_text(t)
print("quality-gate wiring applied (5 points)")
EOF"}

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# declares its own job-level permissions block.

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# declares its own job-level permissions block.

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml')

# 1) needs list: insert installer-portability before installer-verify (keeps the
#    pinned needs tail "install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]" intact)
old = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
new = "supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 2) report line
old = "          echo \"installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}\""
new = old + "\n          echo \"installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}\""
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 3) env var
old = "          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
new = old + "\n          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 4) kv loop: insert before the LAST pair so the pinned tail stays last
old = '                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \\'
new = '                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \\\n' + old
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

# 5) platform class: append to the parenthetical (pinned substring intact)
old = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)"
new = "pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)"
assert t.count(old) == 1
t = t.replace(old, new)

p.write_text(t)
print("quality-gate wiring applied (5 points)")
EOF"}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

    return 1
  fi

  fi

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}
