ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh

#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +

  exit 1
fi

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

content.text:
tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

{{MODE_MENU}}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh

#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.

# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +

  exit 1
fi

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.

So the full-suite run ENDED IN A CRASH — not a pass. This may be:
1. A real native-level crash in pty2 (known class? the repo mentions pty2 exitCode races, ECHILD) — possibly pre-existing on this runner (native heap corruption in the pty C code under load), OR
2. Caused by my IT file (it runs 20+ pty sessions) — but note the crash trace shows tui_protype_snapshot_test, which is NOT my file.

Key question: pre-existing flake or my regression? Evidence needed:
- Did the crash abort the WHOLE run before printing a summary (i.e., "Aborted" killed the dart test process mid-run)? `malloc_consolidate` = heap corruption → abort() kills the process. The tail -20 shows test-name lines then the crash — so yes, the runner died at/after tui_protype_snapshot_test without printing a summary.
- The run order is alphabetical-ish by shard? dart test runs suites concurrently; the crash in tui_protype_snapshot_test (native pty) — this test spawns ptys via pty2 like my IT file.

Was this crash pre-existing? Check: does main have the same behavior? Hard to know without rerunning main (30+ min). Better: rerun JUST the suspicious suite + my suites to see they pass in isolation (they did — 39 tests green repeatedly). A heap-corruption abort under full-suite load in the native pty layer smells like a pre-existing resource/FFI issue (the harness mentions "pty2's own exitCode races the Dart VM's child reaper (ECHILD → -1)" — native fragility is documented).

Practical approach per B7/bounded-fix rule:

2. Instead: check whether this crash reproduces WITHOUT my changes: `git stash` my WIP? My changes are committed (b1a66fe). Run the full suite at HEAD~1 (pre-E3)? The E3 addition is the only delta vs the earlier state — but the crash is in tui_protype_snapshot_test, not my file.

A bare full-suite run may be a genuinely unusual invocation for this repo (nobody runs it bare; the pty suites at full concurrency might trip the native allocator). The malloc crash could be a concurrency artifact.

blocks.text:
PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: origin/main's `tui_protype_snapshot_test.dart` shows the exact same `malloc_consolidate()` abort at VM teardown. My branch did not introduce it. It's a pty2-native heap-corruption-at-exit in the environment's flutter-bundled Dart VM — all tests still PASS; the abort is cosmetic for test results (summary printed before the crash) but makes bare `dart test` exit non-zero mid-run in a full-suite context (the process dies at THAT suite's teardown... wait — in the full run the crash killed the entire `dart test` process before it could finish the remaining suites and print the grand summary).

So: the full bare suite did NOT complete (it aborted in tui_protype_snapshot's teardown partway through the run). That means suites after it never ran. R6 says "run the full test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed". Options:
1. Re-run full suite with `--test-randomize-ordering-seed`? No.
2. Run the full suite EXCLUDING the pre-existing crashing file — `dart test --exclude-tags ...` has no file exclusion; but `dart test <paths>` accepts directory globs... simplest: run the full suite and rely on the fact that the abort kills the process — no.
3. Check if there's a concurrency knob that avoids the corruption (it's a shutdown-time crash in a SPECIFIC suite's VM — actually wait, "tcache_thread_shutdown" in the pair run and "malloc_consolidate" alone — both at process EXIT of the test runner, after all selected tests pass.
